report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward culinary/food/restaurant and general professional/technical/academic vocabulary relative to Model A.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens repeatedly and consistently surface cooking/restaurant terms across many high‑norm cells and positions, especially in later layers: “Cook/Cooking,” “restaurant/Restaurant,” “kitchen/Kitchen,” “baking/Baked/Cake,” “Chef,” “microwave,” “oven,” “culinary,” “pepper,” etc. (e.g., L19–L25, pos1–4).
- The same cells also emphasize professional/technical/academic jargon: “Professional/professional,” “Technical/technical,” “Engineering,” “Innovation,” “dissertation,” “doctoral,” “sciences,” “undergraduate/College,” “molecular,” “laboratory,” “practitioner,” “metropolitan,” “petrochemical.”
- The difference norm is concentrated in mid-to-late layers (peaking dramatically from L20 onward, especially pos1), consistent with a high-level semantic/topic preference rather than a low-level tokenization quirk.

Conclusion: The strongest interpretable change is a domain shift: Model B more strongly favors culinary/recipe/restaurant language and, more broadly, professional/technical/academic terms. I cannot identify a single narrower objective beyond this domain preference from the given evidence.
